frontmatter.name: haiku-worker
frontmatter.description: Fast, cheap execution of mechanical, fully-specified, verifiable tasks — file search and grep, scanning logs or command output, format and text conversion, simple extraction or classification, boilerplate and scaffolding, and deterministic transforms. Delegate here when the task is unambiguous and a wrong answer is cheap to catch. Do NOT use for design, cross-file reasoning, or anything underspecified.

frontmatter.name: opus-worker
frontmatter.description: Hard-reasoning worker. Use for system architecture and design, debugging that spans many files or subsystems, ambiguous or underspecified planning, root-cause analysis, and decisions with high blast radius or that are costly to reverse. Also the right model to run the orchestrator/dispatcher itself. Do NOT use for routine coding — that is the Sonnet worker's job and Opus is overkill there.

frontmatter.name: sonnet-worker
frontmatter.description: Default implementation worker. Handles most real work — feature implementation, refactors within a component, writing and fixing tests, drafting, moderate multi-step reasoning, and standard analysis. The right choice when the task needs genuine judgment but is scoped and not architecturally hard. Prefer this over the Opus worker unless the task is genuinely hard; prefer it over the Haiku worker unless the task is purely mechanical.
